chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said, 'It is like the reward of one who visits Allah above His Throne.'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation / Pilgrimage to a holy site or person

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the high ontological status of the Prophet Muhammad in Shia theology, where his physical presence serves as a divine locus of worship. By equating his visitation with 'visiting Allah above His Throne,' the Imam emphasizes the concept of *tawassul* and the Prophet's role as the ultimate manifestation of Divine proximity, a view supported by the Shi'i interpretation of *Ayat al-Kursi* and *Ayat al-Istawa*.
